cards.explanation: The answer is the forest of the Negev, friends. God tells Ezekiel to "…set your face toward the south, preach against it, and prophesy against the forest of the Negev." (Ezekiel 20:46) Direction AND a target. You know when your phone's map says "turn around when possible" and leaves you to figure out the rest? This is nothing like that.

The answer is a fire, friends. God says, "I am about to ignite in you a fire, and it will devour all your trees…" That's not a little campfire. My oven has one job and it's already enough heat for me.
The answer is False. God says the fire "…will devour all your trees, both green and dry." Green ones don't get a pass, friends. Both kinds are named.
The answer is False. God says, "The blazing flame will not be quenched…" And He says it again in the next verse. Not even my fanciest oven mitts could handle this one, and I take my mitts seriously.

The answer is True. God says, "Then all people will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it will not be quenched." All people will see it, not just a few. And the One they'll see behind it is the LORD.

The answer is that he is just telling parables, friends. Ezekiel says they're saying, "Is he not just telling parables?" (Ezekiel 20:49) He brings it to God right after hearing about a fire that will not be quenched. I think that kind of question would sting.

The answer is Jerusalem. God says, "…set your face against Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries." (Ezekiel 21:2) The fire talk was about the south. Now the word turns to the city itself. Ezekiel keeps getting pointed in new directions, like a man who forgot where he parked.
The answer is His sword, friends. God says, "I am against you, and I will draw My sword from its sheath…" (Ezekiel 21:3) That's a heavy opening line. Nobody needs to wonder where He stands.

The answer is False. God says He will "…cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked." (Ezekiel 21:3) The righteous are named right alongside the wicked. It's a hard verse, friends. I think it's okay to sit quietly with it for a second.

The answer is never. God says, "Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have taken My sword from its sheath, not to return it again." (Ezekiel 21:5) Not to return it again. That's about as final as a sentence gets.

The answer is to groan with a broken heart, friends. God says, "But you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with a broken heart and bitter grief." (Ezekiel 21:6) Most people try to hide their feelings at work. Ezekiel gets told to do the opposite, in public.

The answer is "Because of the news that is coming." When the people ask why he's groaning, that's what Ezekiel is to say. (Ezekiel 21:7) He doesn't give the details in that line. It makes you want to ask what news, doesn't it, friends?

The answer is True. Ezekiel says, "Every heart will melt, and every hand will go limp. Every spirit will faint, and every knee will turn to water." (Ezekiel 21:7) Knees are the part that's supposed to hold you up, friends. When they turn to water, you're not holding anything up.

The answer is False. God says the sword is "…sharpened for the slaughter, polished to flash like lightning!" (Ezekiel 21:10) Nothing about it is for a celebration, friends. It's a heavy part of the passage, and I'll say so plainly.

The answer is False, friends. The verse says the sword is "appointed to be polished, to be grasped in the hand… to be placed in the hand of the slayer." (Ezekiel 21:11) No wall, no display. It's polished to be picked up.

The answer is God's people and Israel's princes. God says, "…the sword is wielded against My people; it is against all the princes of Israel!" (Ezekiel 21:12) The princes of Israel are named right along with His people, friends. That's why Ezekiel is told to cry out and wail.

The answer is closing in on every side. God calls it "…a sword that slays, a sword of great slaughter closing in on every side!" (Ezekiel 21:14) Every side is the phrase the verse uses, friends. I think that's a hard picture to sit with.

The answer is stumble, friends. God says, "So that their hearts may melt and many may stumble, I have appointed at all their gates a sword for slaughter." (Ezekiel 21:15) The sword is appointed at all their gates, so that hearts melt and many stumble. It's a hard verse, and it doesn't hide that.

The answer is to the left. The message says, "Slash to the right; set your blade to the left—wherever your blade is directed." (Ezekiel 21:16) Both directions are named in the verse, friends. Right, then left, wherever the blade is directed.

The answer is that God will strike His hands together, friends. God told Ezekiel, "…prophesy and strike your hands together." (Ezekiel 21:14) and then at the end says, "I too will strike My hands together…" (Ezekiel 21:17) Ezekiel's hands clapping together match what God says He will do. That's a quiet link to catch.

The answer is True. God says, "I too will strike My hands together, and I will satisfy My wrath." (Ezekiel 21:17) Then comes the last line: "I, the LORD, have spoken." That's a serious ending, friends, and the text leaves it plain.
